Here is an example of code for a simple LSTM model for time series classification in Python using the Keras library:

```
from keras.models import Sequential
from keras.layers import LSTM, Dense
import numpy as np

# Prepare your data
# Assume you have X_train and y_train as your training data and X_test, y_test as your testing data
# X_train should have the shape (num_samples, n_timesteps, n_features)
# n_timesteps is the number of time-steps (or observations) in each sample,
# n_features is the number of features in each observation

# Define the LSTM model
model = Sequential()
model.add(LSTM(50, input_shape=(n_timesteps, n_features)))
model.add(Dense(1, activation='sigmoid'))

# Compile the model
model.compile(loss='binary_crossentropy', optimizer='adam', metrics=['accuracy'])

# Fit the model
model.fit(X_train, y_train, epochs=100, batch_size=32, validation_data=(X_test, y_test))

# Make predictions on new data
y_pred = model.predict(X_test)
```
